name: Trichophytic closure

angle.text: Hair transplant patients and surgeons use trichophytic closure after strip harvesting so hair grows through the donor scar, making a short haircut look cleaner. Evidence for the camouflage comes from small comparative studies.

summary: A suturing method that lets hair grow through the donor scar after strip harvesting; evidence is small comparative studies.
note: Applies to strip (FUT) harvesting scars, which remain visible in some cases.
currentQuick:
Trichophytic closure is a way of closing a strip-harvest or facelift incision so hair grows through the scar and hides it.
Studies are small and mostly retrospective.
How it works: Wound edges are trimmed or stepped so follicles survive at the margin and hair grows through the healing scar.
Risks and caveats: It is a surgical closure with usual wound risks; scars can still be visible. Reported scar widths come from a general reference.
deepLead:
Trichophytic closure is a wound-closure technique used after strip (FUT) donor harvesting in hair transplantation and in facelift incisions. Wound edges are prepared so hair can grow through the scar, helping camouflage it.
Published comparisons are small. A 2018 retrospective cohort of 46 rhytidectomy patients compared W-plasty and straight-line trichophytic closure on occipital hairline scars. Other papers describe double or asymmetric suture variants for donor wounds.

name: Platelet-rich fibrin for hair

angle.text: Users and clinics try PRF off-label for thinning hair, as a relative of PRP, hoping growth factors will thicken hair. It is documented mainly in dentistry and oral surgery, and hair-specific research is very limited.

summary: A blood-derived fibrin clot used in dentistry and tried off-label for hair thinning, with almost no hair-specific research.
note: Only a tiny registered trial exists for hair; documented uses are dental.
currentQuick:
Platelet-rich fibrin is made by spinning a person's blood without anticoagulant to produce a platelet and white-cell-rich fibrin clot. It is related to PRP.
Its documented uses are in dental and oral surgery. For hair, one small registered trial comparing it with PRP exists.
How it works: Platelets in the clot release growth factors such as PDGF, TGF-beta and VEGF, and the fibrin matrix acts as a scaffold. Whether this affects hair follicles has not been established in published trials.
Risks and caveats: Risks specific to hair use are not described in the sources reviewed. It is an injection-based aesthetic procedure using the person's own blood.
deepLead:
Platelet-rich fibrin (PRF) is a preparation made from a person's own blood that concentrates platelets and white blood cells in a fibrin matrix. It is described as a derivative of platelet-rich plasma (PRP) and is documented mainly as a tissue-engineering scaffold in oral and maxillofacial surgery . Its use for hair restoration is a newer, off-label application discussed in aesthetic medicine.
Only a very small amount of registered human research exists on PRF for hair: a single listed trial with 10 participants compares PRF and PRP in female pattern hair loss . No results are published in the sources reviewed here.

name: Hair micropigmentation

angle.text: Men with hair loss get scalp micropigmentation to create the look of a buzz cut, add apparent density to a thin crown, or hide transplant scars. The visible result is immediate and is described mainly in press coverage rather than trials.

summary: A scalp tattoo that mimics a buzz cut or camouflages scars; long-lasting, but backed by press coverage rather than studies.
note: Hairline placement matters; removal requires laser.
currentQuick:
Scalp micropigmentation tattoos tiny dots onto the scalp to look like shaved hair follicles. People use it for baldness, thinning density or to hide scars.
It typically takes several sessions and is described as permanent, though touch-ups and laser removal are possible.
How it works: Pigment is placed in the superficial skin, matched to existing hair colour, to imitate the shadow of cropped hair.
Risks and caveats: Allergic reaction to ink is a stated concern, and a poor hairline can look unnatural. No peer-reviewed studies were identified.
deepLead:
Hair micropigmentation, usually called scalp micropigmentation (SMP) or a hair tattoo, is a non-surgical cosmetic tattoo applied to the scalp. It is used to create the look of a closely shaved head on a bald scalp, to add apparent density to a thinning crown, or to conceal hair-transplant scars and other scars on the head .
Wikipedia describes the procedure as typically taking three to four sessions of about two hours each, with pigment matched to the colour of the client's existing hair. It is described as long lasting but removable by laser . The article cites news and magazine coverage rather than peer-reviewed studies .

name: Eyelash implants

angle.text: People seeking permanently fuller lashes consider eyelash transplantation, which places hair into the eyelid margin. It is distinct from extensions and false lashes, and the sources reviewed describe its history but give no outcome studies.

summary: Surgical placement of hair into the eyelids for fuller lashes; sources reviewed give only history, no outcome studies.
note: Surgery on the eyelid; no studies found.
currentQuick:
Eyelash implants are surgical procedures that put hair into the eyelid edge to build lashes. They are distinct from glued-on extensions.
The sources reviewed contain only historical mentions from the 1880s and 1890s.
How it works: Hair is placed into the lid margin so it grows as lashes.
Risks and caveats: Historical accounts describe the early method as painful. No modern safety or outcome studies were found.
deepLead:
Eyelash implants, also called eyelash transplantation, refer to surgical procedures that place hair into the eyelid margin to create or thicken lashes. They differ from temporary eyelash extensions or false lashes, which are applied to or alongside existing lashes.
Sources reviewed here document the history of related practices rather than modern surgical technique. An 1882 report said Parisians had found a way to make false lashes by having hair sewn into the eyelids, and an 1899 newspaper described a painful method of transplanting scalp hair into the eyelids .

name: Artificial hair integrations

chain: Extensions or mesh added to own hair
angle.text: Users with thinning hair or alopecia use weaves, hairpieces and integration systems to add length, volume and coverage right away. The cosmetic result is visible on application; traction and adhesive issues are documented separately.

summary: Extensions, weaves and mesh systems that add hair over thinning areas; reversible, but traction and adhesive problems are documented.
note: Tight braiding can cause traction alopecia.
currentQuick:
Artificial hair integrations blend added human or synthetic hair into the wearer's own hair to add length or cover thinning.
They are non-surgical and reversible, and used for both styling and hair-loss camouflage.
How it works: Added hair is clipped, bonded, sewn or pulled through a mesh base so it merges with existing hair.
Risks and caveats: Prolonged tension can cause traction alopecia, and adhesives are linked to dermatitis and headaches. No clinical trials were found.
deepLead:
Artificial hair integrations are prosthetic hair products, such as extensions, weaves, hairpieces and mesh-based integration systems, that add length, volume or coverage to a person's own hair using human or synthetic fibre. They are used for styling and to camouflage hair loss from conditions such as alopecia .
Wikipedia lists attachment methods including tape-in, clip-in, micro rings, fusion, weaving and wigs, and notes that synthetic fibre such as Kanekalon costs much less than human hair but wears out faster under heat and friction . Reported risks include traction alopecia from tight braiding and skin reactions to adhesives .

name: Scalp cooling cap

angle.text: Chemotherapy patients wear scalp cooling caps to keep more of their hair through treatment. The use is studied in trials, mainly in breast cancer patients; it is a hair-preservation tool rather than a general hair-growth aid.

summary: A cap that chills the scalp during chemotherapy to reduce hair loss; studied mainly in breast cancer patients, with trial support for that use.
note: Studied for chemotherapy-induced hair loss, not general hair loss; not advised with scalp cancer, lymphoma or leukemia.
currentQuick:
A scalp cooling cap lowers scalp temperature during chemotherapy to reduce hair loss. It comes as frozen gel caps or as machine-cooled systems.
It is evaluated mostly in breast cancer patients, including a randomized trial and cohort study published in JAMA in 2017, plus registries and systematic reviews.
How it works: Cooling is thought to reduce blood flow and drug exposure at the hair follicle and slow follicle activity while chemotherapy circulates.
Risks and caveats: Side effects are described as generally minor. Caps are not advised where cancer is in the scalp skin or in lymphoma or leukemia, and a meta-analysis has examined scalp metastasis risk. US costs are roughly $1,500 to $3,000 per course.
deepLead:
A scalp cooling cap is a tight-fitting cap that lowers scalp temperature during chemotherapy, with the aim of reducing chemotherapy-induced hair loss. Caps are either manual gel or ice caps that are frozen beforehand and swapped during treatment, or machine-based systems in which a control unit keeps coolant circulating .
The approach is used mainly by people with cancer rather than in looksmaxxing circles, and its relevance to appearance is the preservation of existing hair during hair-loss-inducing treatment. Randomized and prospective studies in women receiving chemotherapy for breast cancer have examined whether a cooling device reduces hair loss , and systematic reviews have pooled the wider literature .
Wikipedia notes that the procedure is likely to be useful with taxane or anthracycline regimens, that side effects are generally minor, and that caps are not advised where cancer is present in the scalp skin or in lymphoma or leukemia . Costs in the US are described as roughly $1,500 to $3,000 per course .

name: Intralesional corticosteroid scalp injection

angle.text: Dermatologists inject triamcinolone into small patches of alopecia areata, including eyebrow loss, to restore hair in those spots. Reported regrowth is high, though spontaneous remission complicates interpreting the studies.

summary: Steroid injected into patchy hair-loss spots, mainly alopecia areata; reported regrowth is high but spontaneous remission complicates it.
note: Prescription procedure for alopecia areata; spontaneous regrowth is common in small patches.
currentQuick:
Small amounts of corticosteroid, commonly triamcinolone, are injected into patches of alopecia areata or eyebrow loss. It is a clinic-administered prescription treatment.
A 2020 systematic review reported over 50 percent regrowth in about 81 percent of patients at one concentration, though many small patches regrow on their own.
How it works: The steroid acts locally to dampen the immune attack on hair follicles in alopecia areata.
Risks and caveats: The sources reviewed do not detail side effects of the injections. Several registered trials are comparing them with other treatments.
deepLead:
Intralesional corticosteroid injection places a corticosteroid, most often triamcinolone, directly into patches of hair loss. Wikipedia's article on alopecia areata says steroid injections are commonly used where the hair loss areas on the head are small or where eyebrow hair has been lost .
A 2020 systematic review cited by Wikipedia reported more than 50 percent regrowth in 80.9 percent of patients treated with 5 mg/mL triamcinolone injections, while the same article notes that spontaneous remission makes treatment effects hard to judge, with up to 80 percent of people with one or two patches regrowing within a year without treatment .

name: In-office laser whitening

angle.text: People wanting a brighter smile in one visit choose in-office whitening with a light or laser unit. The shade change is visible straight away; whether the light adds anything beyond the gel is still debated.

summary: Peroxide gel on the teeth with a light or laser to speed it up; whether the light adds anything beyond the gel is still contested.
note: Sensitivity is common; colour can partly rebound.
currentQuick:
In-office laser whitening is a dentist-delivered bleaching treatment where a strong peroxide gel is applied and a light or laser unit is aimed at the teeth. Whitening itself is supported by studies; the extra role of the light is debated.
Wikipedia reports typical changes of 2 to 7 shades that can last months, with some rebound in the first week.
How it works: The peroxide gel breaks down stain molecules inside the tooth. Light or laser units are marketed as accelerating that reaction, though a network meta-analysis and other studies have examined whether they improve results over gel alone.
Risks and caveats: Sensitivity is reported by most patients in some studies, lasting days to weeks. Unprotected gums can be burned by strong gels, and heat from light is a reported concern. It is generally provided only by dental professionals.
deepLead:
In-office laser whitening is a professional tooth-bleaching procedure in which a peroxide gel is applied to the teeth and a light source, described by providers as a laser, LED or diode unit, is directed at it to accelerate the colour change. It is delivered by dental staff, with the gums protected by a barrier, and is one of several light-activated in-office options.
Reviews have examined whether the light adds anything. A 2019 systematic review and network meta-analysis asked whether any light-activation protocol improves colour change when combined with an in-office gel. Wikipedia's tooth-whitening article reports that light activation may not outperform high-concentration peroxide alone and that a 2015 study found no improvement and a possible rise in tissue temperature.
Tooth sensitivity is the most commonly reported side effect of in-office bleaching.

name: Zoom whitening

chain: Noticeably whiter teeth in one session
angle.text: Zoom is a branded dentist-applied whitening session people book for a quick, visibly whiter smile, typically before events or other cosmetic work. Shade improvement is routinely recorded, as in other in-office power bleaching.

summary: A branded dentist-applied peroxide-and-light whitening session; shade change is typical, sensitivity common.
note: Sources found are mostly about in-office bleaching generally, not the brand.
currentQuick:
Zoom whitening is a well-known in-office whitening treatment: a dental professional applies strong peroxide gel and uses a light. It is a form of professional power bleaching.
Wikipedia reports changes of 2 to 7 shades for in-office bleaching, lasting months.
How it works: Peroxide gel releases oxidising agents that lighten stain inside enamel and dentin; the lamp is intended to speed the process.
Risks and caveats: Sensitivity is common and usually temporary; gums are protected with a barrier because strong peroxide can burn tissue.
deepLead:
Zoom whitening is the name commonly given to a branded, light-activated in-office tooth-whitening treatment in which a high-strength hydrogen peroxide gel is applied by dental staff and exposed to a lamp. It belongs to the wider category of in-office power bleaching described on Wikipedia, which uses roughly 25-38% hydrogen peroxide with 6-15 minutes of light exposure.
Evidence specific to the branded system is thin in the sources reviewed; research mostly addresses in-office bleaching generally, including how light intensity and peroxide affect sensitivity.

name: Gum depigmentation

chain: Dark gum layer is removed or bleached
Smile looks brighter and more even
angle.text: People with dark, melanin-pigmented gums have them lightened by scalpel, laser or chemical methods for a more even pink gumline. The color change is visible after healing, and support so far is small comparison trials.

summary: Dentist-performed lightening of dark gums by scalpel, laser or chemicals, backed so far by small comparison trials.
note: Evidence is small trials; pigment recurrence is reported inconsistently.
currentQuick:
Gum depigmentation lightens gums that are dark because of melanin, whether from genetics or smoking. It is done as a cosmetic dental procedure.
Most published trials are small and compare one technique against another rather than against no treatment.
How it works: Pigmented surface tissue is removed or ablated by scalpel, laser or chemical agents, and the gum heals with new, lighter tissue.
Risks and caveats: Wikipedia notes a longer recovery after scalpel surgery and possible side effects from chemical methods. Gums heal by secondary intention after laser treatment.
deepLead:
Gum depigmentation is a cosmetic periodontal procedure that lightens dark (melanin-pigmented) gums, using a scalpel, laser or chemical methods. Wikipedia notes that gum pigmentation is mainly linked to genetics and tobacco smoking (smoker's melanosis), with melanin made by melanocytes in the gum's basal layer.
Published clinical trials, mostly small, have compared techniques such as scalpel surgery, diode and Er,Cr:YSGG lasers, microsurgery, bur-based methods and microneedling.

name: Enameloplasty (tooth reshaping)

chain: Dentist shaves small amounts of enamel
angle.text: Users get tooth reshaping to smooth chips, even out edges or tweak tooth length quickly, sometimes in place of braces. The change is immediate and visible; no appearance-focused studies were found.

summary: Dentist shaves tiny amounts of enamel to alter tooth shape; permanent, and no appearance studies were found.
note: Removed enamel does not grow back.
currentQuick:
Enameloplasty is the removal of a little enamel to change how a tooth looks, such as shortening a pointed edge or smoothing a chip.
No clinical studies on the cosmetic use were found; related research concerns sealants and bite adjustment.
How it works: A dentist uses fine instruments to remove and smooth enamel, changing tooth contours.
Risks and caveats: Wikipedia says removed enamel is irreplaceable and that dentin may be exposed.
deepLead:
Enameloplasty, also called tooth reshaping or contouring, is the removal of small amounts of enamel to change a tooth's length, shape or surface, for example to smooth a chip or even out an edge. Wikipedia's cosmetic-dentistry article says it gives fast results and can sometimes stand in for braces, but that removed enamel is irreplaceable and dentin may be exposed.
The term also has clinical uses in the dental literature: widening fissures before placing sealants and adjusting bite surfaces to reduce muscle hyperactivity.

name: Porcelain veneers

angle.text: Veneers are used to change tooth color, shape, size or gaps in one makeover, and are a staple of smile-focused looksmaxxing. The result is plainly visible, and follow-up studies report long-lasting restorations.

summary: Thin ceramic shells bonded to the front of teeth; long-lasting in follow-up studies but they usually require irreversible enamel removal.
note: Enamel removal is generally permanent; costs and longevity vary with dentist and case.
currentQuick:
Porcelain veneers are custom ceramic shells bonded to front teeth to change colour, shape or spacing. They are among the best-studied cosmetic dental restorations, with long-term clinical trials and meta-analyses.
Wikipedia gives lifespans of 10 to 30 years, with chipping, debonding, decay and discoloration as reasons for replacement.
How it works: A dentist usually removes some enamel, takes an impression or scan, and a lab makes the shells, which are etched and bonded to the tooth with resin cement.
Risks and caveats: Reported risks are sensitivity, decay, debonding and fracture; preparation can remove a meaningful part of the tooth surface, and critics argue veneers are overused. Costs are substantial.
deepLead:
Porcelain veneers are thin, custom-made shells, usually of porcelain or glass-ceramic, bonded to the front of teeth to change their colour, shape, size or spacing. They are made indirectly by a dental technician, unlike composite veneers, which can be built directly in the mouth.
A 2016 meta-analysis of clinical trials on feldspathic porcelain and glass-ceramic laminate veneers examined survival and complications including debonding and fracture, and a ten-year prospective trial followed 87 veneers in 25 patients. Wikipedia reports lifespans of 10 to 30 years with modern bonding, with reasons for replacement including chipping, discoloration and decay, and notes that preparation can remove tooth structure.

name: Maryland bridge

angle.text: People missing a tooth use a Maryland bridge to fill the gap with little drilling of neighboring teeth. The gap is visibly closed once placed, and debonding is the usual failure noted in the literature.

summary: A winged bridge glued to neighbouring teeth to replace a missing tooth with little drilling; debonding is the usual failure.
note: Not suited to grinders, mobile teeth or nickel allergy.
currentQuick:
A Maryland bridge replaces a missing tooth, often a front tooth, using a false tooth with wings glued behind the adjacent teeth.
It preserves more natural tooth than a conventional bridge because little preparation is needed.
How it works: The wings are bonded to acid-etched enamel on the lingual surface of neighbouring teeth, holding the pontic in the gap.
Risks and caveats: Debonding is the main concern and can let decay start under a loose wing; contraindications include grinding, mobile teeth and nickel allergy.
deepLead:
A Maryland bridge, also called a resin-bonded or adhesive bridge, replaces a missing tooth with a pontic that has metal or ceramic 'wings' bonded to the etched enamel of neighbouring teeth, requiring little or no preparation of them. Its name is noted on Wikipedia, which has no history section for it.
It is discussed in the appearance context mainly as a conservative way to replace a missing front tooth. Wikipedia states that debonding is the main failure concern, that cantilever single-retainer designs have fewer complications than designs bonded on both sides, and that contraindications include bruxism, mobile teeth and nickel allergy.

name: Gum graft

chain: Gum tissue moved over exposed roots
angle.text: Gum grafts are done mainly for recession, and some seek them to cover exposed roots and even out the gumline for a better smile. The surgical result is visible once healed; the cosmetic use is secondary to the dental one.

summary: Surgery that moves gum tissue over exposed roots; used for recession and sometimes for looks, with donor-site pain the main reported downside.
note: Donor-site pain is the most commonly reported unwanted effect.
currentQuick:
A gum graft covers exposed tooth roots or thickens thin gum by moving tissue from the palate, from next to the tooth, or from a processed donor matrix. It is mainly a periodontal treatment for recession, with a cosmetic side when front teeth look long.
A literature review summarised on Wikipedia reported recession was reduced after most root coverage procedures, and registered trials continue to compare techniques.
How it works: Tissue is placed over the exposed root and sutured so it heals in place; variants differ in where the tissue comes from (palate, adjacent gum, donor matrix or blood-derived fibrin).
Risks and caveats: Reported effects are discomfort and pain, mainly at the palatal donor site, plus possible donor-site recession with pedicle grafts and healing or disease-transmission considerations with donor matrices.
deepLead:
A gum graft, also called gingival grafting or periodontal plastic surgery, is a family of surgical procedures in which gum tissue is moved or added to cover exposed tooth roots or to thicken a thin band of gum . It is most often performed by periodontists, and the usual reason is gum recession, in which the gum margin has migrated away from the crown and exposed the root surface .
Recession can cause sensitivity and may make teeth, particularly the front teeth, look longer, so some patients seek grafting partly or mainly for appearance . The same source notes that untreated recession is not by itself a direct cause of tooth loss and that not all recession requires surgery . In looksmaxxing-adjacent discussion the procedure appears as a hardmaxx-category dental option for gumline aesthetics.
Clinical trials registered on ClinicalTrials.gov compare graft techniques, donor-site healing and patient experience, and a 2018 literature review summarised on Wikipedia reported that recession was reduced after most root coverage procedures, with pain at the palatal donor site the most common unwanted effect .

name: Gum lift

angle.text: Users with a gummy smile or short-looking teeth have the gumline reshaped to show more tooth, overlapping with crown lengthening. The change is visible after healing; evidence specific to cosmetic use is thin.

summary: Reshaping the gumline, sometimes with bone, to show more tooth; evidence for cosmetic use is thin and bone removal is permanent.
note: Removed bone cannot generally be restored.
currentQuick:
A gum lift reshapes the gumline to expose more tooth, either for functional dental reasons or to rebalance a gummy smile. It is closely related to crown lengthening.
No registered trials directly study cosmetic gum lifts; published encyclopedic sources describe the technique and its trade-offs.
How it works: A periodontist lifts the gum, may reshape bone to a lower level and repositions the flap, or alternatively uses braces to extrude the tooth.
Risks and caveats: Bone removal is irreversible and can weaken neighbouring support and complicate implants; the gum margin may drift back toward the crown, and soreness typically lasts one to two weeks.
deepLead:
A gum lift is the cosmetic term for reshaping the gumline to expose more of the tooth, a procedure that overlaps with crown lengthening . Crown lengthening is a surgical procedure, usually performed by a periodontist, that exposes more tooth by removing some gum tissue and sometimes supporting bone .
It has functional uses, such as improving retention for a crown or reaching decay below the gumline, and aesthetic uses such as adjusting gum-to-tooth proportions in a gummy smile . Cosmetic dentistry sources describe gum contouring as making teeth look longer or more even . Wikipedia's crown lengthening article does not use the term gum lift .
Bone removal is irreversible, and the gum margin may gradually shift back toward the crown after surgery . No trial in the registered set examined cosmetic gum lifts directly; registered gum-surgery trials concern recession coverage.

name: Internal bleaching

angle.text: People with a single darkened root-canal-treated tooth, often at the front, use internal bleaching to match it to the rest of the smile. Reports describe high immediate success, with some re-treatment needed.

summary: Whitening a darkened root-canal-treated tooth from the inside; reported high immediate success, with resorption risk and some re-treatment.
note: Cervical root resorption is a documented risk, especially with heat-activated methods.
currentQuick:
Internal bleaching lightens a dark, root-canal-treated tooth by sealing a peroxide-based agent inside it and changing it over successive visits.
A critical review reported over 90% immediate success, with 10 to 40% of treated teeth needing re-treatment within 1 to 8 years.
How it works: Hydrogen peroxide, or compounds that release it such as sodium perborate and carbamide peroxide, breaks down the pigment inside the tooth.
Risks and caveats: Cervical root resorption is the main documented concern, more often with thermocatalytic methods; dentine weakening and crown fracture have also been described.
deepLead:
Internal (intracoronal) bleaching is a tooth-whitening procedure for root-canal-treated, non-vital teeth, which lose their nerve supply and often darken . The bleaching agent is sealed inside the tooth rather than applied to the outer surface, and is replaced every few weeks until the desired shade is reached; it is most often done on front teeth .
Present techniques rely on hydrogen peroxide, applied directly or produced from sodium perborate or carbamide peroxide . A critical review reported more than 90% immediate success for intracoronal bleaching of non-vital teeth, with 10 to 40% of successfully treated teeth needing re-treatment over 1 to 8 years .
Cervical root resorption is the best-documented serious risk, linked especially to heated (thermocatalytic) methods .

name: Bite reclamation

chain: Longer teeth and fuller lower face
angle.text: Those with teeth worn down by grinding or acid use bite reclamation to rebuild height, which can make the lower face look less shortened. It is part of full-mouth reconstruction; sources are thin and no trials were found.

summary: Rebuilding worn teeth to restore bite height; sources are thin and no trials were found.
note: Large restorative work; little published evidence located.
currentQuick:
Bite reclamation reopens a bite that has collapsed from tooth wear, to restore the height of the lower face. It is described as part of complex full-mouth reconstruction.
Only brief encyclopedic descriptions were found; no trials.
How it works: Worn teeth are rebuilt so the jaws meet at a greater vertical dimension.
Risks and caveats: Sources describe the work as complex; no safety data specific to the procedure were found.
deepLead:
Bite reclamation is a term used in cosmetic dentistry for reopening the bite to restore vertical dimension lost through wear, such as from grinding or acid reflux, which can make the lower face look shortened . It is described as part of full-mouth reconstruction, complex work involving many teeth .
Vertical dimension of occlusion is the up-and-down relationship of the jaws when the teeth meet, and dental references describe a deficient vertical dimension as giving a collapsed look with the chin close to the nose . Sources found for this entry are encyclopedic summaries only; no published trial on bite reclamation was located.

name: Wax-up smile mock-up

chain: Model or temporaries of planned teeth
Preview shows size, shape, smile line
Final veneers match the chosen look
angle.text: Patients planning veneers use a wax-up or mock-up to see proposed tooth changes against their lips and smile before committing. The preview itself is visible and testable in the mouth; published sourcing is thin.

summary: A model or temporary preview of planned tooth changes, used before veneers; thin sourcing.
note: Preview only; sources are thin.
currentQuick:
A wax-up or mock-up previews planned cosmetic tooth changes so patient and dentist can judge size, shape and proportion before treatment.
Only a short encyclopedic description and one registered digital smile design trial were found.
How it works: A model or temporary is shaped to the planned result and tried against the lips and smile line, sometimes also testing speech and bite.
Risks and caveats: The preview itself is non-permanent; the sources describe no specific risks of the mock-up.
deepLead:
A wax-up or mock-up is a diagnostic preview in cosmetic dentistry: dentists build a model of planned tooth changes to guide preparation before veneers are made . It shows how changes in tooth size, shape and proportion will relate to the gums, lips and smile line, and temporaries based on it can test appearance, speech and bite before final work .
Digital smile design is a related, software-based approach. One registered crossover study of 44 participants compares AI-assisted with conventional digital smile design for laminate veneers; it is active and not yet reporting results .

name: Surgical orthodontics

chain: Jaw bone is cut and repositioned
angle.text: Looksmaxxers consider jaw surgery with braces to correct bite, airway and facial imbalance, including recessed or overlong jaws. It is established medicine, and the changes in jaw position and profile are visible afterward.

summary: Jaw surgery coordinated with braces to correct bite and facial proportions; established medicine with real surgical risks and long recovery.
note: Major surgery: infection, numbness and weeks to months of recovery are reported.
currentQuick:
Surgical orthodontics combines braces with jaw surgery to correct bite problems, airway issues and facial balance. Surgeons reposition the upper jaw, lower jaw or chin, usually through the mouth.
It is established medical practice, and studies report high post-surgical satisfaction alongside temporary low mood in some patients.
How it works: Orthodontists align the teeth, and an oral and maxillofacial surgeon cuts and repositions jaw bone, fixing it with plates and screws; some patients have surgery first.
Risks and caveats: Reported risks include bleeding, swelling, infection and facial numbness that usually recovers within about three months; initial healing takes 2 to 6 weeks and bone union a further 2 to 4 months.
deepLead:
Surgical orthodontics usually refers to orthodontic treatment combined with orthognathic (corrective jaw) surgery, in which a surgeon cuts, moves and realigns jaw bone to correct bite problems, airway issues and facial imbalance, typically through the mouth and in coordination with an orthodontist . The term is also used for surgically facilitated orthodontics, such as corticotomy, which aims to speed tooth movement .
Indications include skeletal jaw discrepancies, underbites, overbites, open bites, receding chins, sleep apnea, temporomandibular joint problems and facial asymmetry . Appearance is among the stated goals, and surgery can improve facial aesthetics and self-esteem according to Wikipedia's summary .
Risks include bleeding, swelling, infection and facial numbness from nerve injury, which is usually temporary . Psychological studies from the 1980s reported depressive reactions in some patients during recovery, alongside high satisfaction later .

name: All-on-4

chain: Four implants hold a full arch
angle.text: People with failing teeth choose All-on-4 to get a full fixed arch in a new, uniform smile, which looksmaxxing culture files under hardmaxx dental work. It is established dental surgery with high reported survival, aimed at tooth loss rather than facial change.

summary: Full-arch fixed teeth on four implants; established dental surgery with reported high survival, but pricey and aimed at tooth loss, not facial change.
note: Manufacturer-funded early research; prosthetic wear and bone loss reported.
currentQuick:
All-on-4 replaces a whole arch of teeth with a fixed bridge held by four implants, two of them angled to avoid grafting. Teeth are usually fitted within about a day of surgery.
In looksmaxxing circles it is discussed as a dental "hardmaxx" for people with failing or missing teeth. Long-term data come largely from the originating clinic and manufacturer-linked studies; independent trials are small.
How it works: Titanium implants fuse with the jaw bone. The tilted rear implants use denser front bone and avoid sinus and nerve areas, and a bridge screwed onto the implants is worn full-time.
Risks and caveats: Reported issues include wear of acrylic teeth, bone loss around implants, infection and implant failure. Costs are high and vary widely by country.
deepLead:
All-on-4 is a prosthodontic treatment concept in which a full arch of missing teeth is replaced by a fixed prosthesis supported by four dental implants, the rear two usually tilted so they can be anchored without bone grafting. The prosthesis is typically fitted within about 24 hours of surgery, and "All-on-4" is a trademark of the implant manufacturer Nobel Biocare. It is classed in looksmaxxing culture as a "hardmaxx" dental procedure because it is sometimes pursued to replace failing teeth with a new, uniform smile.
The concept was developed by the Portuguese prosthodontist Paulo Maló and colleagues and named in the early 2000s, building on earlier work on tilted and immediately loaded implants. Published follow-up studies from Maló's group report high implant survival over several years, although much of the early research was funded by the manufacturer.
This article records what is reported about the procedure. Entries in the ClinicalTrials.gov registry show that comparative trials of framework materials and implant configurations are ongoing, and no registered trial examined here was designed around facial appearance as an outcome.
